title: CBR encoding + mux rate for stable IPTV playback on any hardware
description: On high-power machines the stream plays in extreme fast forward. Root cause: CRF (VBR) encoding of static/logo content produces near-zero bitrate; IPTV players drain the receive buffer faster than realtime when data rate is very low. This is masked on CPU-limited boxes but exposed on .97 (beefier AMD). Fix: switch to VBV CBR (-b:v = -minrate = -maxrate) with a -muxrate on the MPEG-TS output. CBR ensures constant data rate regardless of content complexity or CPU speed.
close_reason: CBR VBV encoding (-b:v == -minrate == -maxrate) + -muxrate on MPEG-TS output. Verified identical constant output rate on both .98 and .97. CRF removed from UI and encoder. dev-deploy.sh now supports MV_HOST override.

title: Lock multiview output audio to its source video (no A/V drift)
description: Next focus. The PyAV worker paces the selected channel(s) audio (resampled 48k s16, silence fallback) and the video (latest-frame per tile) independently against the worker's wall clock, so effective latencies can differ (decode latency, skip_frame=NONREF, buffering) and clocks can drift over a long session -> lip-sync drifts off. GOAL: output audio stays locked to its source channel's video indefinitely, at all costs. Approach to investigate: drive audio + the audio source's video from the SAME source PTS instead of independent wall-clock pacing; a bounded jitter buffer (a couple seconds behind live is acceptable per user) to align with a fixed delay; drift correction (insert/drop samples or resample) for long-term lock; handle audio_source single vs all and silence fallback without losing alignment. Acceptance: lip-sync holds over a long run across auto/featured/top_featured layouts. Files: src/compositor_worker.py (Channel audio decode + audio_feeder + video pacing in main()). Related: multiview-c5n (passthrough drops extra tracks).
close_reason: PTS-anchor at startup + flush on reconnect; wall-clock pacing retained for smooth output

title: server.py seamless multiview rebuild
description:
Rebuild the streaming core of src/server.py so the multiview composite starts instantly with channel logos and each tile seamlessly swaps its placeholder for live video, never stalling the composite. Architecture: per-tile persistent encoder + broadcast-style identical-param TS splice at a keyframe. Composition reads N always-on normalized tile streams. Plan: ~/.claude/plans/indexed-mixing-moth.md

## Context
Survivor of a buggy rebuild (HEAD 8ed2161 'blow it all up'). Old failures: gevent/ffmpeg stdout bridging churn, and xstack stall from byte-splicing different-parameter TS. config.py/layouts.py/epg.py/__init__.py stay untouched.
notes: 2026-06-24: Fixed long-term instability (stutter/slow-mo creep). Sources are all 1080p60; we output 30fps, so decoding every frame wasted ~half the decode and the box (i7-10750H, 12 threads) saturated over time (load ran away to 13.3+, a tile's decode collapsed 102->27fps). FIX: vs.codec_context.skip_frame=NONREF (skip non-reference/B frames at decode -> ~30fps of ref frames, matching output) + decode thread_count 4->3 + cap ffmpeg encoder -threads 4. RESULT over a 170s run: load plateaus ~11/12 (was runaway), per-channel decode stable ~26-37fps the whole time (no collapse), 0 corruption, clean sharp picture at 150s. CPU headroom is tight (~11/12) for one multiview on this box; concurrent multiviews would need more. Created bead multiview-0kg for package.sh vendoring (download amd64+arm64 wheels, package both, detect platform in-code, keep out of git).
close_reason: Rebuild shipped: replaced the splice/xstack design with a PyAV worker (per-channel decode -> numpy compose -> libx264 ffmpeg encode). Working in Dispatcharr: ~1.1x realtime, clean, resilient, load ~7/12. Remaining/forward work tracked by standalone beads (M3U bug e9s.9, audio sync, hardware epic, deps install).

title: Audio desync accumulates across stream reconnects
description: When an unstable channel disconnects and reconnects (flashing back to the placeholder logo briefly), audio slowly drifts out of sync with video over time. Each reconnect appears to introduce a small offset that compounds. The placeholder flash itself is acceptable; the desync is the bug. Need to investigate whether the compositor re-anchors PTS correctly on reconnect, or whether the audio/video clock drifts relative to each other each time a channel recovers.

title: Fix intermittent plugin load failure (KeyError/ModuleNotFoundError on reload)
description: During Dispatcharr plugin reload cycles, importlib.import_module relative imports in _config(), _server(), _epg(), and _deps() fail because they require the parent package (_dispatcharr_plugin_multiview) to be in sys.modules at call time. On fast machines with multiple Celery workers or retried discovery, that entry is missing or evicted, producing KeyError or ModuleNotFoundError. Fix: replace relative imports with file-path-based loading via importlib.util.spec_from_file_location in a shared _load_submodule() helper.
close_reason: Replaced all importlib.import_module relative imports with file-path-based _load_submodule() helper in src/__init__.py

title: Mitigate resource leaks and add memory diagnostics
description: Production streams stay up for ~1hr but Dispatcharr web UI goes unresponsive. Root causes: audio_w FDs not closed before enc.wait() (so ffmpeg hangs and enc.kill() fires instead), enc_out_r not closed after ffmpeg exits, AudioResampler not explicitly closed on reconnect, no memory diagnostic in heartbeat log, _drain_stderr greenlet not tracked/killed on stream end, _body() in _serve_realsrc has no explicit finally to close live_stream() generator, and _mv_keepalives dict is never initialized at module level. Fix all of these and add RSS logging to heartbeat so we can confirm whether memory growth is the actual cause.
close_reason: Closed

title: Dynamic tile reflow when a channel exhausts reconnect retries
description:
When a Channel.run() thread exits after RECONNECT_RETRIES consecutive failures it sets self.dead=True. The compositor loop should detect this and reflow the surviving tiles to fill the canvas using tile_rects() from layouts.py, exactly as if the layout had been configured with one fewer channel from the start.

Design (fully planned, ready to implement):

server.py: add 'layout' key to the cfg dict returned by _worker_config() so the worker knows which layout type to use for reflow.

compositor_worker.py changes:
1. Import: from layouts import tile_rects as _tile_rects
2. Channel.__init__: store self._logo_url = spec.get('logo') and self.dead = False. Start logo thread using self._logo_url instead of local variable.
3. Channel.run(): after the 'giving up' log line, set self.dead = True before break.
4. New Channel.resize(x, y, w, h): update self.x/y/w/h, replace self.fallback and self.latest with black_planes(w, h), set self.fresh_until=0.0, start a new _load_logo background thread for the new size.
5. main() compositor loop: maintain active=list(channels); at the top of each frame check live=[c for c in active if not c.dead]; if len changed, call _tile_rects(layout_type, len(live), out_w, out_h), call c.resize(x,y,w,h) for each survivor, reassign active=live; if active is empty, break.
6. Frame compositing loop: add shape safety check before writing to canvas -- if Yt.shape != (t.h, t.w): use black_planes(t.w, t.h) instead. Handles the brief race window where a surviving channel's run() thread writes an old-sized frame between resize() and the next decoded frame.

Audio: pipes are fixed at subprocess startup. Dead audio channels continue writing silence via take() returning zeros. Audio track count in MPEG-TS stays constant -- no change needed.

Backoff schedule for reference: 2+4+8+16+32+60*7 = ~8 min before giving up and triggering reflow.

title: Exponential backoff with max retries for channel reconnect
description: Channel.run() retries failed connections forever with a fixed 2s sleep. Need exponential backoff starting at 2s, capped at 60s, giving up after N consecutive failures. Failure counter resets when a connection delivers at least one decoded video frame, so a channel that drops mid-stream gets a fresh slate of retries.
close_reason: Closed

title: Fix placeholder logos: path, aspect ratio, alpha, early composite
description: Logo placeholders were broken and slow to appear. Four issues fixed: (1) _channel_logo() used ch.logo.url but Logo is a custom model with an HTTP URL, not a Django FileField -- the old _usable_logo() filter rejected all HTTP URLs so logos were never passed to the worker. Fix: pass the URL directly to av.open() which handles HTTP natively. (2) _make_fallback() scaled logos to a square (side x side) regardless of actual dimensions. Fix: fit within a w/3 x h/3 bounding box preserving aspect ratio. (3) RGBA decode used np.frombuffer(bytes(plane)) which breaks when PyAV pads plane rows for alignment -- reshape error for non-aligned widths. Fix: use frame.to_ndarray(format='rgba'). (4) Logo loading was synchronous in Channel.__init__(), blocking the compositor from starting until all logos were fetched. Fix: background thread per channel swaps self.fallback when ready; compositor starts immediately with black frames.
close_reason: Fixed in compositor_worker.py (_make_fallback, _load_logo) and server.py (_channel_logo)

title: NVIDIA: h264_nvenc encode (decode/NVDEC as sub-task)
description: First hardware target. ENCODE: use h264_nvenc in the worker's ffmpeg encoder when video_encoder=h264_nvenc; restore NVENC config fields (preset p1-p7, cq); detect NVIDIA (/dev/nvidia*, nvidia-smi). Big CPU win (offloads libx264). DECODE sub-task: PyAV hwaccel cuda/nvdec for the child decoders - investigate the GPU->CPU download cost vs the CPU decode it saves (numpy compose needs CPU frames). NOTE: dispatcharr-test has no NVIDIA GPU; needs a different test box.
notes: Starting point: the video_encoder dropdown and per-encoder field builders (_nvenc_fields, _qsv_fields, _vaapi_fields) were stripped from config.py and server.py to ship the CBR/rate-limiter fix cleanly; recover them from git history (commit cbdb658 or earlier has the full set). The encoder subprocess is build_encoder_cmd() in compositor_worker.py; swap the libx264 block for h264_nvenc. For NVENC, check for /dev/nvidia* in the container and pass --gpus or -v /dev/nvidia* when starting (check how dispatcharr-test is launched on .97). The video_encoder setting flows from server._worker_config() into the cfg dict consumed by compositor_worker. Decode hwaccel (NVDEC) is a separate sub-task and lower priority; numpy compositing requires frames in CPU memory so any GPU-decoded frame must be downloaded back (av.VideoFrame.to_ndarray() does this but negates much of the decode benefit unless compositing moves to GPU).

title: Ship code-only; install/update PyAV on demand via a plugin action (per platform)
description: Dispatcharr caps plugin import at DISPATCHARR_PLUGIN_IMPORT_MAX_BYTES (default 200MB). One vendored PyAV arch is ~114MB; two ~228MB > limit, so bundling wheels in the zip does not fit. NEW APPROACH (supersedes 'package both arches'): do NOT ship deps. Ship a tiny code-only zip and install PyAV at runtime on the Dispatcharr host via plugin ACTION buttons. Implement: src/deps.py (detect_arch, pyav_status, install_pyav(arch) that fetches the matching cp313 manylinux wheel from the PyPI JSON API via urllib - container has no pip - and unpacks into vendor/<arch>/); __init__.py actions install_pyav_amd64 / install_pyav_arm64 + run() dispatch; worker fails loudly telling the user to run the action; package.sh stops bundling wheels and excludes vendor from the zip (keep --revendor for local dev only); vendor stays gitignored. Needs host internet (PyPI) + write access to the plugin dir.
notes: 2026-06-24: IMPLEMENTED + verified. src/deps.py (detect_arch, pyav_status, install_pyav via PyPI JSON API + urllib + zipfile, no pip). __init__.py: 'Install PyAV (amd64/arm64)' actions + run() dispatch + a dynamic 'Media Engine (PyAV)' status info field. server._serve_stream: 503 with a clear 'run Install PyAV' message if PyAV missing for the host arch. worker: clearer import-error message. package.sh: stops bundling wheels, excludes vendor from the zip (-x '*/vendor/*'), --revendor for local dev only; made bash-3.2 portable (no declare -A). Result: release zip is 60K (was ~228MB, over the 200MB limit). Verified on dispatcharr-test: removed vendor -> install action (run as the 'dispatch' user) downloads+unpacks PyAV 14.2.0 from PyPI -> streaming works, 0 decode errors. GOTCHA fixed: docker-cp deploys land files as root but Dispatcharr runs as 'dispatch'; the plugin dir must be dispatch-owned for the action to write vendor/ (real installs are fine; dev-deploy.sh now chowns after sync).

title: Verification pass: unit + local smoke + in-Dispatcharr
description: Unit: tsutil splicer. Local smoke: stub realsrc with ffmpeg test source, run MultiviewServer standalone, ffprobe/VLC /stream/1, confirm instant logos + seamless swap + composite survives a killed realsrc. In Dispatcharr: package.sh, upload, VLC a multiview channel, check logs for no xstack stall, kill an upstream source -> tile shows offline card while others play.
notes:
Done locally: (1) tsutil unit tests 8/8 pass; (2) real ffmpeg smoke - placeholder and live tile produce byte-identical params/PIDs (h264 1280x720 @30000/1001 PID0x100, ac3 48k stereo PID0x101); (3) real splice via tsutil - video decodes clean through the splice, CC 0 discontinuities, only one ac3 block glitch at the boundary (recovers). Remaining: in-Dispatcharr test requires uploading multiview-dev-454a81e2 zip and a live channel (user step).
In-Dispatcharr test #1 found a bug: dispatcharr.live_stream and the tile/realsrc routes used the integer channel PK, but Dispatcharr's live proxy keys channels by UUID (url_utils get_object_or_404(Channel, uuid=channel_id)). Fixed: thread the channel uuid through _resolve_layout -> tile/realsrc URLs -> dispatcharr.live_stream; classic-mode settings still store the int pk and we resolve it to uuid. Repackaged: multiview-dev-23da99c4.
In-Dispatcharr test #2 (via ssh logs): UUID fix confirmed working (TSN1/TSN2 spliced to live cleanly). But the multiview OUTPUT channel got 0/4 chunks for 10s and Dispatcharr aborted it (CONNECTION_TIMEOUT), cascading teardown. Root cause: placeholder encoders had no -re, so lavfi sources flooded frames; with composition wallclock timestamps this gave non-monotonic/clustered DTS and stalled the output muxer (no bytes during the placeholder-only phase). Fix: added -re to placeholder lavfi/logo inputs (matches the old working design). Also bumped live-tile probe to 5M/5M so audio is detected reliably (TSN3 appeared audioless -> live failed -> correctly stayed on placeholder, which is PMT-safe). Repackaged 23da99c4 (123759).
Test #3: -re fixed the muxer stall, but composition still timed out. Logs showed it opens tile inputs SEQUENTIALLY, ~5s find_stream_info per input (in#0 @30.4, in#1 @33.3, in#2 @39.5); Dispatcharr killed the output channel at 34.2 before input 2 even opened. Fix: composition inputs now use analyzeduration/probesize 500000 (0.5s) since tiles are known h264+ac3/fixed-PID format, plus -flush_packets 1 on output. Should open all inputs in ~1.5-2s. Repackaged 124344. Not multithreading - the serialization was ffmpeg's internal sequential probe.
Test #4 reproduced LOCALLY with a gevent harness (real MultiviewServer+TilePipeline, stubbed live source). Root cause of 'no data': composition opened the 3 tile inputs SERIALLY, each waiting ~1.5s for its placeholder to spawn-on-connect, then xstack waited for the wallclock-misaligned inputs to overlap -> first output byte at 7.94s, past Dispatcharr's 10s budget after overhead. Fixes: (1) pre-warm all tile pipelines concurrently at /stream time via a token registry (TilePipeline -> gevent Queue, drained by /internal/tile/{token}) so placeholders are spawned+aligned before composition connects; (2) read1() instead of read(CHUNK) in _pump_stdout and pipeline pumps so available bytes forward immediately; (3) analyzeduration/probesize 100000 + -flush_packets 1. Result: first byte 2.54s, ~7.3Mbps real-time, valid 1080p, tiles splice to live (verified by decoding a frame). Repackaged 125900.
Test #5 (build 125900): startup-timeout FIXED - stream stays up 60s+, no teardown, TSN1/TSN2 splice to live. Remaining: choppy video + 'waits for children'. Container CPU ~62% of 12 cores (745% across 7 ffmpeg: composition 312%, 2 live re-encodes ~195% each), output channel stayed healthy (no underrun warnings). Local harness (clean+delayed sources) produces perfectly smooth 30fps even across the splice, so choppiness is real-source-specific (network jitter / sub-realtime live re-encode), not the splice itself. Tried moving wallclock to tile encoders + dropping composition wallclock -> splice STALLS (composition wallclock is needed to mask the splice timeline mismatch); reverted. Shipped diagnostic build 131630 with per-tile and composition output-rate logging to determine if it's low fps (CPU) vs jittery delivery.
Test #6 diagnosis: live tiles delivered in 10-24s BURSTS while sources were healthy (60fps/8Mbps). Root cause = too much encoding (per-tile re-encode x3 + composition = 4 software encodes), composition couldn't hold realtime, multi-stage buffer chain oscillated. Per user decision, PIVOTED to single-ffmpeg architecture: one ffmpeg reads channels directly via /internal/realsrc, layout filter scales/fps-normalizes each, single encode. Removed tile registry/_serve_tile/_run_tile/TilePipeline usage; added dispatcharr.prewarm (concurrent channel init) and wallclock on composition inputs for cross-channel sync; audio map now optional (fixes audioless channels). Local: smooth (frames all 0.0334s), first byte ~1.1s, 1 encode. Repackaged 133005. Seamless splice preserved as backlog multiview-e9s.10 (hw-encoder-gated).

title: Fix audio track code for channels with mixed-case names (e.g. Rogers TV Kitchener -> rtv)
description:
## Problem

_lang_code() in src/server.py produces 'tv' for 'CA | Rogers TV Kitchener' because it finds all-uppercase words only ('TV'), joins them, and ignores the mixed-case words. The result is not representative of the channel.

## Fix

Replace the sig+fallback two-branch logic with a single rule: expand each word in full if it is an all-uppercase abbreviation (len >= 2), otherwise take its first letter. This gives 'R' + 'TV' + 'K' = 'RTVK'[:3] = 'rtv'.

## Acceptance criteria

- 'CA | Rogers TV Kitchener' produces 'rtv' not 'tv'
- Pure-acronym single-word channels (ESPN, TSN) unchanged
- Channels where all sig words already dominate (CTV News Channel -> ctv) unchanged
close_reason: Closed

title: EPG forward: pass through raw XMLTV instead of re-mapping custom_properties
description:
## Problem

The current EPG forward mode re-emits only title, sub_title, and description from ProgramData. Everything else that Dispatcharr stores -- live, previously_shown, premiere, categories, season/episode, rating, credits, icon, images, language, etc. -- lives in custom_properties as a parsed JSON blob. Re-emitting it faithfully would require hardcoding a JSON-key-to-XMLTV-tag mapping that mirrors (and must stay in sync with) Dispatcharr's extract_custom_properties() logic.

## Proposed approach

Store the raw inner XML of each <programme> element on ProgramData at parse time (a new field, e.g. raw_xml TextField). When forwarding, just emit the stored XML with the channel attribute rewritten to multiview_N. No mapping needed, no information lost, and no coupling to Dispatcharr internals.

When emitting, append the list of channels in the layout to the programme description (either as the last line of an existing <desc>, or as a new <desc> if none is present). This preserves the "what's on this tile" context that the current placeholder mode provides.

## Acceptance criteria

- ProgramData gains a raw_xml field (migration required)
- Dispatcharr EPG parser captures inner XML of each <programme> at parse time and stores it
- epg.py forward mode emits raw_xml with channel attribute rewritten, falling back to the current title/subtitle/desc path if raw_xml is absent (for existing rows or providers that dont store it)
- live, categories, episode, rating, and other fields survive round-trip through the multiview EPG
- The layout's channel list is appended to the description in the emitted XMLTV (last line of existing <desc>, or a new <desc> if the programme has none)

title: Define match priority when a channel hits multiple regex layouts
description: When a channel name matches the regex pattern of more than one multiview layout, it is currently tiled in all matching layouts. It is unclear whether this is the intended behavior or whether each channel should belong to at most one layout. If exclusive ownership is desired, a 'first match wins' or 'last match wins' policy needs to be defined and exposed as a setting. This is a design/clarification question before any implementation.

title: EPG source options for regex-matched channels: dummy EPG or forward from a specific channel
description: Add per-layout EPG source options, available in both classic and regex selector modes. Two new options: (1) a 'dummy' mode that emits a minimal placeholder program entry (current behavior, make it explicit), and (2) a 'forward from channel' mode that copies the EPG from a user-selected source channel onto the multiview layout's XMLTV output. Also: in regex mode, clarify/expose whether 'first' or 'last' match wins when a channel matches multiple regex layouts.
close_reason: Added epg_source_mode (dummy/forward) per layout in config.py and epg.py. Forward mode queries ProgramData from the selected channel and emits real XMLTV entries, falling back to dummy if no data. Available in both classic and regex modes. Regex multi-match resolution split to multiview-dx7.

title: Fix startup port-bind race on fast multi-worker hosts
description: On .97 (fast AMD+NVIDIA box), multiple Dispatcharr celery workers start simultaneously and all race to bind port 9292, producing 'Address already in use' errors in logs. On .98 (slower) this doesn't manifest because worker startup is naturally staggered. The server should only start once (the first worker to claim the port wins; others detect it's already up). Also related: compositor threads request channel URLs before Dispatcharr's live_proxy has warmed up the channels, causing 'Invalid data found when processing input' on the first 2-3 connection attempts per channel; this self-heals via RECONNECT_BACKOFF=2s but causes ~6s of logo display at stream start. Both issues are in src/server.py (startup) and src/compositor_worker.py (channel reconnect). The port-bind race may already be partly handled by the OSError check in MultiviewServer.start() but logs show it still fires multiple times.
notes: 503-fix deployed to .97 on 2026-06-24: _serve_realsrc now peeks the live_stream generator before committing to 200 OK; returns 503 if the proxy isn't ready yet, so PyAV gets a clean 5XX and retries via exponential backoff instead of seeing 'Invalid data'. Remaining open: port-bind race (multiple celery workers racing to bind 9292).

title: VAAPI: h264_vaapi encode (AMD/Intel) (decode as sub-task)
description: VAAPI hardware encode (h264_vaapi) for AMD/Intel via /dev/dri/renderD128; restore vaapi_device config field. Decode (vaapi) as a sub-task with the GPU->CPU caveat. The dispatcharr-test box has an Intel iGPU (/dev/dri/renderD128) so VAAPI is testable there.
notes: Starting point: recover _vaapi_fields from git history (commit cbdb658). VAAPI encode uses h264_vaapi; requires /dev/dri. Both test hosts have /dev/dri (Intel iGPU on .98, AMD on .97). Command pattern: ffmpeg -vaapi_device /dev/dri/renderD128 -vf 'format=nv12,hwupload' -c:v h264_vaapi. Unlike NVENC, VAAPI needs explicit pixel format conversion before hwupload since rawvideo input is yuv420p.

title: Intel QSV: h264_qsv encode (decode as sub-task)
description: Intel Quick Sync hardware encode (h264_qsv) in the worker's ffmpeg encoder; restore QSV config fields; detect /dev/dri. Decode (qsv) as a sub-task with the same GPU->CPU caveat.
notes: Starting point: same as multiview-61o.1 - recover _qsv_fields from git history (commit cbdb658). QSV encode uses h264_qsv; requires /dev/dri in container. Test host: seth@192.168.1.98 (Intel i7-10750H has Intel UHD 630 iGPU, /dev/dri/renderD128 present). Verify with: docker exec dispatcharr-test ls /dev/dri/ and vainfo. QSV may need -init_hw_device qsv=hw:/dev/dri/renderD128 or similar in the ffmpeg cmd.

title: Vendored dependency (PyAV) version & update management
description: Pin + update the PyAV dependency now that it is installed on demand (see 0kg) rather than committed. (1) Pin exact version/python-tag/manylinux in src/deps.py; (2) the 'Install/Update PyAV' plugin action doubles as the update mechanism (re-fetch newer pinned version); (3) guard against Dispatcharr changing Python version/arch - worker fails loudly if no matching wheel; (4) track upstream PyAV releases for ffmpeg security fixes and bump the pin. The 'in git vs build-time' question is resolved (neither: on-demand install).

title: Optional seamless per-tile splice mode (needs hardware encoder)
description: The seamless logo->live per-tile splice (instant placeholders, no wait for channels, seamless join) requires re-encoding every tile plus the composition = ~N+1 simultaneous encodes. On CPU/libx264 this is too heavy (measured ~745% CPU for 3 tiles and choppy/bursty output), so v1 shipped the lighter single-ffmpeg architecture (1 decode/channel + 1 encode, reads channels directly). Backlog: make the seamless splice an OPTIONAL mode the user can enable WHEN a hardware encoder (NVENC/QSV/VAAPI) is configured/available, where the per-tile re-encodes are cheap. The implementation already exists in pipeline.py + tsutil.py (TS splicer, validated by unit tests) and the old build_placeholder_cmd/build_live_tile_cmd in ffmpeg.py - gate it behind a setting + hardware-encoder detection. Also revisit: instant logo placeholders for the single-ffmpeg mode (logo-until-ready overlay).
acceptance_criteria: A config toggle (auto-enabled only with a hw encoder) selects seamless per-tile splice; falls back to single-ffmpeg otherwise. Seamless mode shows instant logo placeholders and seamless join without choppiness on a hw-encoder box.
close_reason: Superseded: per-tile TS-splice architecture abandoned (pipeline.py/tsutil.py removed). Hardware support reborn as the new hardware-acceleration epic.

title: Investigate M3U refresh ProgrammingError (CREATE TABLE / psycopg) during generate_m3u
description: celery refresh_single_m3u_account -> cleanup_streams -> streams_to_delete.delete() raises psycopg ProgrammingError 'the last operation didn't produce records (command status: CREATE TABLE)'. Surfaced when our generate_m3u triggers the M3U refresh. Looks like a DB connection-state issue inside Dispatcharr's m3u task (possibly gevent/psycopg connection reuse or test-env DB state), not the streaming path. Confirm whether it's reproducible without our plugin / pre-existing in Dispatcharr; if ours, find what about our M3U account write triggers it.
notes: 2026-06-24 ROOT CAUSE + FIX (verified). The error 'parsing failed: the last operation didn't produce records (command status: INSERT 0 84)' was caused by OUR generate_m3u action firing TWO celery tasks at once: refresh_epg_data.delay() (from epg.generate_epg) AND refresh_single_m3u_account.delay(). They ran concurrently on Dispatcharr's threaded celery pool sharing a psycopg DB connection (Dispatcharr even calls _release_task_db_connection() trying to isolate it). The M3U task's final query saw the EPG task's command status (INSERT 0 84 = the 84 multiview EPG programs) and raised ProgrammingError. The M3U data actually updated but the account was marked ERROR. It is a Dispatcharr concurrency bug but we provoked it. FIX: serialize the two refreshes via a celery chain in dependency order, M3U first (creates channels) then EPG (maps programs). epg.generate_epg now returns the EPGSource id instead of auto-firing; __init__._generate_m3u calls _refresh_m3u_then_epg() which fires chain(refresh_single_m3u_account.si(account_id), refresh_epg_data.si(source_id)). VERIFIED on dispatcharr-test: full plugin action -> M3U refresh completes with no error -> EPG refresh runs after; M3U account status=SUCCESS ('Processing completed in 0.5s. Streams: 0 created, 1 updated'). The INSERT 0 N / ProgrammingError is gone.
close_reason: Fixed: serialized our M3U+EPG refresh triggers (celery chain, M3U then EPG) so they no longer collide on Dispatcharr's shared DB connection. Verified: account status SUCCESS, no ProgrammingError.

title: Splice audio glitch: one ac3 block corrupt at placeholder->live boundary
description: Splicing on a video keyframe leaves one ac3 frame straddling the boundary malformed (ffmpeg logs 'invalid coupling range', then recovers, ~32ms). Video is clean. Optional polish: also align the splice to an audio frame boundary, or mute/crossfade one frame. Low priority; cosmetic.
close_reason: Superseded: no placeholder->live splice boundary in the PyAV-worker architecture.
